title: Ice and Rain Protection — Wing Anti-Ice — One Time Cold Travel Time Measurement of the Shut-Off Valves
abstract: A one time cold travel time measurement of the wing anti-ice shut-off valves, used to rank aircraft for conversion so that the worst are converted in the first winter rather than at the end of the programme.

sections.planning_reason: The conversion programme for the wing anti-ice shut-off valves runs over thirty months and operators need to know which of their aircraft are most exposed in the first winter. Recorded travel times at ambient temperature do not discriminate: the marginal aircraft look normal until the seal is cold. A measurement taken after a defined cold soak separates the population clearly, and the fleet sample used to develop the modification showed a bimodal distribution with roughly one aircraft in five sitting in the slow group.
sections.description: This Service Bulletin gives the instructions for a one time measurement of the opening travel time of each wing anti-ice shut-off valve after a defined cold soak period, and for the recording and reporting of the result. No hardware is changed. The measurement uses the valve travel gauge and the existing position switch signal, taken at the valve connector rather than at the flight deck, so that the indication delay is excluded. Aircraft whose measured time exceeds the reporting threshold on either wing are to be scheduled for conversion in the first available slot.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Leave the aircraft cold soaked with the leading edge unheated for the period stated in the procedure, and record the ambient and the surface temperature at the valve. Open the leading edge access panels. Connect the travel gauge at the valve connector in accordance with AMM-T-30-10-11-000-001-A. Command the valve open and record the time from command to the position signal transition, for each of the four valves, without cycling the valve beforehand. Close the leading edge panels. Report the four measured times, the soak period and the recorded temperatures to the manufacturer using the reporting form. Where any measured time exceeds the reporting threshold, schedule the aircraft for the modification bulletin at the first available opportunity and record the result in the aircraft file.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to Auran powered TITAN-88 aircraft in the MSN T00001 to T00166 range that have not yet embodied the high force solenoid standard. An aircraft already converted has nothing to measure and is outside the effectivity.
sections.material_note: No kit and no parts are required. The travel gauge is a common tool already required by the modification bulletin, and operators without one may borrow it from the regional pool. The reporting form is issued with this bulletin.

type_data.compliance_time: Before the start of the first winter operating season after the date of this Service Bulletin.
